points.place: 威斯康星州里奇兰中心
points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 赖特出生于威斯康星州的一个牧师家庭，童年时期经常接触自然景观和建筑工地。他的母亲安娜·劳埃德·赖特是一位教师，鼓励他对艺术和建筑的兴趣。这段时期，赖特接触了福禄贝尔积木，这种几何形状的玩具对他后来的建筑理念产生了深远影响。1885年，他进入威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校学习工程，但两年后辍学，前往芝加哥寻求建筑实践机会。
points.descriptionEn: Born to a preacher's family in Wisconsin, Wright's childhood was immersed in natural landscapes and construction sites. His mother, Anna Lloyd Wright, a teacher, nurtured his interest in art and architecture. During this period, Wright was exposed to Froebel blocks, geometric building blocks that profoundly influenced his later architectural philosophy. In 1885, he enrolled at the University of Wisconsin-Madison to study engineering but dropped out after two years, heading to Chicago to pursue architectural practice.

points.title: 学徒时期
points.description: 1888年，赖特进入芝加哥著名的建筑公司阿德勒与沙利文事务所工作，担任路易斯·沙利文的助理。这段经历让他接触到了高层建筑设计的最新技术，并深受沙利文'形式追随功能'理念的影响。1893年，由于被发现在独立承接项目而违反公司规定，赖特被迫离开事务所。尽管如此，这段时期他参与了芝加哥许多重要建筑的设计，包括芝加哥百货公司大楼，这些经历为他后来的独立职业生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1888, Wright joined the prestigious firm Adler & Sullivan in Chicago, working as an assistant to Louis Sullivan. This period exposed him to cutting-edge techniques in high-rise design and deeply influenced by Sullivan's 'form follows function' philosophy. In 1893, Wright was forced to leave the firm after being caught taking on independent projects, violating company policy. Despite this, he contributed to many significant Chicago buildings during this time, including the Chicago Auditorium Building, experiences that laid the foundation for his independent career.

points.title: 草原风格
points.description: 离开阿德勒与沙利文事务所后，赖特在芝加哥郊区的橡树园建立了自己的工作室。这一时期，他发展出了标志性的'草原风格'建筑，强调水平线条、开放平面设计和与自然环境的融合。他设计了超过150栋住宅，包括著名的罗比住宅和马丁住宅。这些作品摒弃了维多利亚时期的繁复装饰，转而采用简洁的几何形式和有机材料，开创了美国现代建筑的先河。1909年，赖特的生活出现转折，他与客户埃德温·切尼的妻子玛莎·博顿私奔，导致他的婚姻破裂和职业生涯危机。
points.descriptionEn: After leaving Adler & Sullivan, Wright established his own studio in Oak Park, a Chicago suburb. During this period, he developed his iconic 'Prairie Style' architecture, emphasizing horizontal lines, open floor plans, and integration with the natural environment. He designed over 150 homes, including the famous Robie House and Martin House. These works rejected Victorian-era ornamental details in favor of clean geometric forms and organic materials, pioneering American modern architecture. In 1909, Wright's life took a turn when he eloped with Martha 'Mamah' Borthwick Cheney, the wife of his client Edwin Cheney, leading to the collapse of his marriage and career crisis.

points.title: 重建与探索
points.description: 1911年，赖特在威斯康星州的斯普林格林建造了他的家和工作室塔里埃森（Taliesin），这个名字源自威尔士神话中的'闪亮额头'。1914年，悲剧降临，一名家庭仆人纵火焚烧了塔里埃森，并杀害了玛莎和另外四人。这场灾难后，赖特重建了塔里埃森，并在此期间发展了新的建筑理念。1915年，他接受日本任务，设计了东京的帝国酒店，该建筑以其抗震设计而闻名，使他在国际建筑界获得声誉。
points.descriptionEn: In 1911, Wright built his home and studio Taliesin in Spring Green, Wisconsin, a name derived from Welsh mythology meaning 'shining brow'. Tragedy struck in 1914 when a domestic servant set fire to Taliesin, killing Mamah and four others. After this disaster, Wright rebuilt Taliesin and developed new architectural concepts during this period. In 1915, he accepted a commission in Japan, designing the Imperial Hotel in Tokyo, which became famous for its earthquake-resistant design, earning him international acclaim in the architectural world.

points.title: 晚年杰作
points.description: 1937年，赖特在亚利桑那州斯科茨代尔建造了他的冬季住宅和工作室塔里埃森西（Taliesin West）。这一时期，他创作了职业生涯中最具影响力的作品，包括纽约的古根海姆博物馆（1959年开放）、宾夕法尼亚州的流水别墅（1937年）和加州的索伦住宅。他的建筑理念更加成熟，强调'有机建筑'概念，认为建筑应该与自然环境和谐共存。赖特晚年获得了多项荣誉，包括1949年美国建筑师学会金奖，并在1959年4月9日在塔里埃森西去世，享年91岁，留下了超过1000个已完成的设计作品。
points.descriptionEn: In 1937, Wright built his winter home and studio Taliesin West in Scottsdale, Arizona. During this period, he created his most influential works, including the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York (opened 1959), Fallingwater in Pennsylvania (1937), and the Salk Institute in California. His architectural philosophy matured, emphasizing the concept of 'organic architecture'—the idea that buildings should exist in harmony with their natural environment. In his later years, Wright received numerous honors, including the AIA Gold Medal in 1949. He died on April 9, 1959, at Taliesin West at age 91, leaving over 1,000 completed designs.

points.title: 西海岸影响
points.description: 1923年至1925年间，赖特在洛杉矶工作，为好莱坞精英设计了多座住宅。这一时期，他适应了西海岸的生活方式，设计了更加开放、流动的空间，如著名的霍利霍克住宅（1923年）。这些作品体现了他对加州气候和生活方式的理解，将草原风格与加州的现代主义相结合。赖特在洛杉矶的作品影响了一代建筑师，包括后来的现代主义大师理查德·诺伊特拉和鲁道夫·辛德勒，为加州现代建筑的发展奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1923 and 1925, Wright worked in Los Angeles, designing numerous homes for Hollywood elites. During this period, he adapted to West Coast lifestyles, creating more open, flowing spaces like the famous Hollyhock House (1923). These works reflected his understanding of California's climate and lifestyle, blending Prairie Style with California modernism. Wright's Los Angeles projects influenced a generation of architects, including later modern masters Richard Neutra and Rudolph Schindler, laying the foundation for California modern architecture.

appraisal.zh: 赖特被公认为美国最伟大的建筑师之一，其有机建筑理念改变了人们对建筑与自然关系的理解，草原风格与流水别墅、古根海姆博物馆等作品影响深远，他本人也不只是建筑师，更是借建筑表达民主与人与自然和谐理想的思想者。另一种看法认为，他的实践争议明显：常超预算、误工期，古根海姆博物馆即严重超支；个人生活多有婚外情与私奔；有时忽视结构工程原理致建筑出现功能缺陷；作品过于个人化而难以复制，对国际风格的排斥也使他一度被主流建筑界边缘化。
appraisal.en: Wright is widely regarded as one of America's greatest architects: his organic architecture changed how buildings relate to nature, the Prairie Style and works such as Fallingwater and the Guggenheim left a lasting mark, and he was a thinker who used building to express ideals of democracy and harmony with nature. Another view holds that his practice was plainly controversial: budgets and deadlines were routinely overrun, notably at the Guggenheim; his personal life was marked by affairs and elopements; he sometimes neglected structural principles, producing functional flaws; and his highly personal work resisted replication, while his rejection of the International Style left him marginalized until late in life.

supporter.zh: 赖特被誉为美国最伟大的建筑师之一，他的'有机建筑'理念彻底改变了人们对建筑与自然关系的理解。他打破了传统建筑的束缚，创造了独特的空间体验，强调建筑应与环境和人类生活和谐共存。赖特的草原风格和后来的作品影响了全球现代建筑发展，他的流水别墅和古根海姆博物馆等作品被视为建筑艺术的杰作。他不仅是一位建筑师，更是一位思想家，通过建筑表达了他对民主、自由和人与自然和谐共处的理想。
supporter.en: Wright is celebrated as one of America's greatest architects, whose 'organic architecture' philosophy revolutionized understanding of the relationship between buildings and nature. He broke free from traditional architectural constraints, creating unique spatial experiences that emphasized harmony between structures, their environment, and human life. Wright's Prairie Style and later works influenced global modern architecture, with masterpieces like Fallingwater and the Guggenheim Museum considered pinnacles of architectural art. More than just an architect, he was a thinker who expressed his ideals of democracy, freedom, and harmony between humans and nature through his buildings.

critic.zh: 赖特的设计理念和实践也存在明显争议。他经常超出预算且延误工期，如古根海姆博物馆的建设就超支严重。他的个人生活充满争议，包括多次婚外情和私奔行为。在专业上，他有时忽视结构工程原理，导致某些建筑出现功能性缺陷。此外，他的作品被认为过于个人化，难以大规模复制，限制了其理念的广泛传播。赖特对现代主义国际风格的排斥也使他一度被主流建筑界边缘化，直到晚年才重新获得认可。
critic.en: Wright's design philosophy and practices faced significant criticism. He frequently exceeded budgets and deadlines, with the Guggenheim Museum construction becoming notoriously over budget. His personal life was controversial, marked by multiple affairs and elopements. Professionally, he sometimes overlooked structural engineering principles, leading to functional issues in some buildings. Additionally, his work was considered too personalized for mass replication, limiting the widespread adoption of his ideas. Wright's rejection of the International Style of modernism also marginalized him from mainstream architectural circles until his later years.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，赖特被定义为美国现代建筑的开创者之一，他的影响超越了建筑领域，成为美国文化的重要象征。他的'草原风格'住宅代表了美国中产阶级理想的物质表达，而他的有机建筑理念则反映了美国对自然和自由的独特理解。赖特的作品在流行文化中频繁出现，从电影到广告，成为美国现代性的视觉标志。尽管他的个人生活充满争议，但他的建筑遗产持续影响着当代建筑师，他的'塔里埃森'建筑学校至今仍在培养新一代建筑师，延续了其设计理念。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Wright is defined as a pioneer of American modern architecture, whose influence extends beyond architecture into American cultural symbolism. His Prairie Style homes represented the material expression of American middle-class ideals, while his organic architecture philosophy reflected America's unique relationship with nature and freedom. Wright's work frequently appears in popular culture, from films to advertisements, becoming a visual icon of American modernity. Despite his controversial personal life, his architectural legacy continues to influence contemporary architects, and his Taliesin architectural school still trains new generations in his design principles.

self.zh: 建筑是自然与人类之间和谐的媒介，是生活艺术的最高形式。
self.en: The mother art is architecture. Without an architecture of our own we have no soul of our own civilization.
